target_disjoint_workload.question: For each quota usage record with a positive in-use amount, list the quota usage ID, project ID, and resource type, along with the number of linked reservations and the total reserved delta across those reservations (only including reservations that expired before 2021-11-16 19:30:59). Also show, for that resource type, the variance and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of reservation delta values, compute the average reserved delta per reservation, and include the overall average reserved delta per reservation across all such usage records as a benchmark. Finally, categorize each usage record as 'HIGH_AVG_DELTA' (at least 50% above the benchmark), 'LOW_AVG_DELTA' (at least 50% below the benchmark), or 'AVERAGE_AVG_DELTA', ordering by delta variance descending.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH UsageReservationStats AS (SELECT q.ID AS usage_id, q.PROJECT_ID, q.RESOURCE, COUNT(r.ID) AS reservation_count, SUM(r.DELTA) AS total_reserved_delta FROM `quota_usages` AS q JOIN `reservations` AS r ON q.ID = r.USAGE_ID WHERE q.IN_USE > 0 AND r.EXPIRE < '2021-11-16 19:30:59' GROUP BY q.ID, q.PROJECT_ID, q.RESOURCE), ResourceDeltaDispersion AS (SELECT qu.RESOURCE AS resource, VARIANCE(r.DELTA) AS delta_variance, STDDEV(r.DELTA) AS delta_stddev FROM `quota_usages` AS qu JOIN `reservations` AS r ON qu.ID = r.USAGE_ID WHERE qu.DELETED = 0 AND r.EXPIRE < '2021-11-16 19:30:59' GROUP BY qu.RESOURCE ORDER BY delta_variance DESC) SELECT urs.usage_id, urs.PROJECT_ID, urs.RESOURCE, urs.reservation_count, urs.total_reserved_delta, rdd.delta_variance, rdd.delta_stddev, ROUND(urs.total_reserved_delta / NULLIF(urs.reservation_count, 0), 2) AS Avg_Reserved_Delta_Per_Reservation FROM UsageReservationStats AS urs JOIN ResourceDeltaDispersion AS rdd ON urs.RESOURCE = rdd.resource ORDER BY rdd.delta_variance DESC), Benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(Avg_Reserved_Delta_Per_Reservation) AS benchmark_avg_reserved_delta_per_reservation FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.usage_id, i.PROJECT_ID, i.RESOURCE, i.reservation_count, i.total_reserved_delta, i.delta_variance, i.delta_stddev, i.Avg_Reserved_Delta_Per_Reservation, b.benchmark_avg_reserved_delta_per_reservation AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.Avg_Reserved_Delta_Per_Reservation > b.benchmark_avg_reserved_delta_per_reservation * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_AVG_DELTA' WHEN i.Avg_Reserved_Delta_Per_Reservation < b.benchmark_avg_reserved_delta_per_reservation * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_AVG_DELTA' ELSE 'AVERAGE_AVG_DELTA' END AS avg_delta_category FROM inner_cte AS i CROSS JOIN Benchmark AS b ORDER BY i.delta_variance DESC

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each project and resource among quota usage records that have a positive in-use amount, show the project ID, resource type, and whether the project has any “high reservation” usage (where the total reserved delta across linked reservations exceeds the in-use amount). Also return the number of usage records, total reservations, and total reserved delta. Include subtotals per project and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT q.ID AS usage_id, q.PROJECT_ID, q.RESOURCE, COUNT(r.ID) AS reservation_count, SUM(r.DELTA) AS total_reserved_delta FROM `quota_usages` AS q JOIN `reservations` AS r ON q.ID = r.USAGE_ID WHERE q.IN_USE > 0 GROUP BY q.ID, q.PROJECT_ID, q.RESOURCE), ProjectResourceStatus AS (SELECT i.PROJECT_ID, i.RESOURCE, CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM `quota_usages` AS q2 JOIN inner_cte AS i2 ON i2.usage_id = q2.ID WHERE q2.IN_USE > 0 AND q2.PROJECT_ID = i.PROJECT_ID AND q2.RESOURCE = i.RESOURCE AND i2.total_reserved_delta > q2.IN_USE) THEN 'High' ELSE 'Normal' END AS reservation_pressure, COUNT(DISTINCT i.usage_id) AS usage_records, SUM(i.reservation_count) AS total_reservations, SUM(i.total_reserved_delta) AS total_reserved_delta FROM inner_cte AS i GROUP BY i.PROJECT_ID, i.RESOURCE, reservation_pressure) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(PROJECT_ID) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE PROJECT_ID END AS project_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(RESOURCE) = 1 AND GROUPING(PROJECT_ID) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE RESOURCE END AS resource, CASE WHEN GROUPING(reservation_pressure) = 1 AND GROUPING(RESOURCE) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(reservation_pressure) = 1 AND GROUPING(RESOURCE) = 1 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE reservation_pressure END AS reservation_pressure, SUM(usage_records) AS usage_records, SUM(total_reservations) AS total_reservations, SUM(total_reserved_delta) AS total_reserved_delta FROM ProjectResourceStatus GROUP BY PROJECT_ID, RESOURCE, reservation_pressure WITH ROLLUP

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each quota resource type, show the minimum quota usage ID and the average reservation delta for non-deleted quota usage records (q.DELETED = 0) where the reservation resource is either 'cores' or 'instances', and also include how that average reservation delta deviates from the overall average reservation delta across all such records. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT MIN(q.ID) AS min_usage_id, AVG(r.DELTA) AS avg_reservation_delta FROM `quota_usages` AS q JOIN `reservations` AS r ON q.ID = r.USAGE_ID WHERE q.DELETED = 0 AND r.RESOURCE IN ('cores', 'instances') GROUP BY q.RESOURCE), overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(r.DELTA) AS overall_avg_reservation_delta FROM `quota_usages` AS q JOIN `reservations` AS r ON q.ID = r.USAGE_ID WHERE q.DELETED = 0 AND r.RESOURCE IN ('cores', 'instances')) SELECT i.min_usage_id, i.avg_reservation_delta, (i.avg_reservation_delta - oa.overall_avg_reservation_delta) AS deviation_from_overall_avg FROM inner_cte AS i CROSS JOIN overall_avg AS oa

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each quota usage record, return the quota usage ID, its resource type, and the total reserved delta from its linked reservations, considering only reservations that expired before 2021-11-16 19:30:59 and only non-deleted quota usages; include only those quota usages where the total reserved delta is more than one standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) above the mean reservation delta across all (filtered) reservations. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT qu.ID AS usage_id, SUM(r.DELTA) AS total_reserved_delta FROM `quota_usages` AS qu JOIN `reservations` AS r ON qu.ID = r.USAGE_ID WHERE r.expire < '2021-11-16 19:30:59' GROUP BY qu.ID HAVING SUM(r.DELTA) > (SELECT AVG(DELTA) + STDDEV(DELTA) FROM `reservations` WHERE expire < '2021-11-16 19:30:59')) SELECT inner_cte.usage_id, qu.RESOURCE AS usage_resource, inner_cte.total_reserved_delta FROM inner_cte JOIN `quota_usages` AS qu ON qu.ID = inner_cte.usage_id WHERE qu.DELETED = 0

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each quota resource type, show the resource name and compute the average and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the reservation delta values for reservations linked to that quota usage, considering only reservations that expired before 2021-11-16 19:30:59. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: SELECT qu.RESOURCE AS resource, AVG(r.DELTA) AS avg_reservation_delta, STDDEV(r.DELTA) AS reservation_delta_stddev FROM `quota_usages` AS qu JOIN `reservations` AS r ON qu.ID = r.USAGE_ID WHERE qu.DELETED = 0 AND r.EXPIRE < '2021-11-16 19:30:59' GROUP BY qu.RESOURCE ORDER BY reservation_delta_stddev DESC

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each quota resource type, list the resource name along with the average and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of reservation delta values, and only include resources where the average reservation delta is greater than 10% of the quota’s in-use amount. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT qu.RESOURCE AS resource, AVG(r.DELTA) AS avg_reservation_delta, STDDEV(r.DELTA) AS reservation_delta_stddev FROM `quota_usages` AS qu JOIN `reservations` AS r ON qu.ID = r.USAGE_ID WHERE qu.DELETED = 0 GROUP BY qu.RESOURCE ORDER BY reservation_delta_stddev DESC) SELECT inner_cte.resource, inner_cte.avg_reservation_delta, inner_cte.reservation_delta_stddev, AVG(qu.IN_USE) AS avg_in_use FROM inner_cte JOIN `quota_usages` AS qu ON qu.RESOURCE = inner_cte.resource AND qu.DELETED = 0 WHERE inner_cte.avg_reservation_delta > 0.10 * qu.IN_USE GROUP BY inner_cte.resource, inner_cte.avg_reservation_delta, inner_cte.reservation_delta_stddev ORDER BY inner_cte.avg_reservation_delta DESC

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each quota resource type, show the resource name and the geometric mean of reservation deltas for reservations linked to that quota usage (considering only reservations where the delta is greater than 0), but return only those resources whose geometric mean is greater than the overall average geometric mean across all resources. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT q.RESOURCE AS resource, EXP(AVG(LN(r.DELTA))) AS geometric_mean FROM `quota_usages` AS q JOIN `reservations` AS r ON q.ID = r.USAGE_ID WHERE r.DELTA > 0 GROUP BY q.RESOURCE ORDER BY geometric_mean DESC) SELECT resource, geometric_mean FROM inner_cte WHERE geometric_mean > (SELECT AVG(geometric_mean) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY geometric_mean DESC

target_disjoint_workload.question: How many compute nodes have the QEMU hypervisor type, are linked to a resource provider (matching on UUID), and belong to aggregate ID 1? Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS qemu_compute_nodes_with_resource_provider FROM `compute_nodes` AS cn JOIN `resource_providers` AS rp ON cn.UUID = rp.UUID JOIN `aggregate_hosts` AS ah ON ah.HOST = cn.HOST WHERE cn.HYPERVISOR_TYPE = 'QEMU' AND ah.AGGREGATE_ID = '1'

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group and rule protocol, list the security group name, description, project ID, the rule protocol, and the number of non-deleted rules. Also include subtotals per security group and a grand total, considering only non-deleted groups and rules. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME, sg.DESCRIPTION, sg.PROJECT_ID, sgr.PROTOCOL, sgr.FROM_PORT, sgr.TO_PORT, sgr.CIDR, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sg.ID ORDER BY sgr.ID) AS window_column FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.DELETED = 0 AND sgr.DELETED = 0), RuleCounts AS (SELECT NAME, DESCRIPTION, PROJECT_ID, PROTOCOL, COUNT(*) AS total_rules FROM inner_cte GROUP BY NAME, DESCRIPTION, PROJECT_ID, PROTOCOL) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(NAME) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE NAME END AS security_group_name, CASE WHEN GROUPING(DESCRIPTION) = 1 AND GROUPING(NAME) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE DESCRIPTION END AS security_group_description, CASE WHEN GROUPING(PROJECT_ID) = 1 AND GROUPING(NAME) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE PROJECT_ID END AS project_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(PROTOCOL) = 1 AND GROUPING(NAME) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE PROTOCOL END AS protocol, SUM(total_rules) AS total_rules FROM RuleCounts GROUP BY NAME, DESCRIPTION, PROJECT_ID, PROTOCOL WITH ROLLUP

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group name and its TCP “from port” variability status (High if the from-port range is at least 1000, otherwise Low)—including subtotals per security group name and a grand total—show the total number of security groups in that category and how many qualifying (non-deleted) security group rules belong to that security group where the security group’s id is greater than the average id across all non-deleted security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH sg_tcp_from_port_variability_rollup AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, MAX(sgr.FROM_PORT) - MIN(sgr.FROM_PORT) AS from_port_range, VARIANCE(sgr.FROM_PORT) AS from_port_variance FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.NAME ORDER BY from_port_range DESC), RangeStatus AS (SELECT security_group_name, CASE WHEN from_port_range >= 1000 THEN 'High' ELSE 'Low' END AS variability_status, COUNT(*) AS total_security_groups FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_name, variability_status) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(security_group_name) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE security_group_name END AS security_group_name, CASE WHEN GROUPING(variability_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(security_group_name) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE variability_status END AS variability_status, SUM(total_security_groups) AS total_security_groups FROM RangeStatus GROUP BY security_group_name, variability_status WITH ROLLUP), sg_rule_details_with_max_next_2 AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME, sgr.PROTOCOL, sgr.FROM_PORT, sgr.TO_PORT, sgr.CIDR, sgr.ID AS RULE_ID, MAX(sg.ID) OVER (ORDER BY sgr.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING) AS MAX_GROUP_ID_NEXT_2 FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.DELETED = 0) SELECT i.NAME, i.PROTOCOL, i.FROM_PORT, i.TO_PORT, i.CIDR, i.RULE_ID, i.MAX_GROUP_ID_NEXT_2 FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN `security_groups` AS sg2 ON sg2.NAME = i.NAME WHERE sg2.DELETED = 0 AND sg2.ID > (SELECT AVG(sg3.ID) * 1.0 FROM `security_groups` AS sg3 WHERE sg3.DELETED = 0)) SELECT v.security_group_name, v.variability_status, v.total_security_groups, COUNT(r.RULE_ID) AS qualifying_rule_count FROM sg_tcp_from_port_variability_rollup AS v LEFT JOIN sg_rule_details_with_max_next_2 AS r ON r.NAME = v.security_group_name GROUP BY v.security_group_name, v.variability_status, v.total_security_groups ORDER BY v.security_group_name, v.variability_status

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group and tcp-rule CIDR, list the security group ID, name, and description, the CIDR, and the number of tcp rules and total TO_PORT across those rules. Include subtotals per security group and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.ID AS security_group_id, sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sg.DESCRIPTION AS security_group_description, COUNT(sgr.ID) AS rule_count, SUM(sgr.TO_PORT) AS total_to_port FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.ID, sg.NAME, sg.DESCRIPTION), CidrBreakdown AS (SELECT sg.ID AS security_group_id, sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sg.DESCRIPTION AS security_group_description, sgr.CIDR AS cidr, COUNT(sgr.ID) AS cidr_rule_count, SUM(sgr.TO_PORT) AS cidr_total_to_port FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID JOIN inner_cte AS i ON i.security_group_id = sg.ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.ID, sg.NAME, sg.DESCRIPTION, sgr.CIDR) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(security_group_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE security_group_id END AS security_group_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(security_group_name) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE security_group_name END AS security_group_name, CASE WHEN GROUPING(security_group_description) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE security_group_description END AS security_group_description, CASE WHEN GROUPING(cidr) = 1 AND GROUPING(security_group_id) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(cidr) = 1 AND GROUPING(security_group_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE cidr END AS cidr, SUM(cidr_rule_count) AS rule_count, SUM(cidr_total_to_port) AS total_to_port FROM CidrBreakdown GROUP BY security_group_id, security_group_name, security_group_description, cidr WITH ROLLUP

target_disjoint_workload.question: For the security group named "aurum-xenon", return only those rules whose from-port is greater than the average from-port for their protocol, and for each such rule show the security group name, description, user ID, project ID, protocol, from port, to port, CIDR, the minimum from port over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following rule rows (ordered by the parent group ID), the rule’s deviation from the overall average from port across all "aurum-xenon" rules, and the running sum of from ports within the same protocol ordered by from port. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH q1 AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME, sg.DESCRIPTION, sg.USER_ID, sg.PROJECT_ID, sgr.PROTOCOL, sgr.FROM_PORT, sgr.TO_PORT, sgr.CIDR, MIN(sgr.FROM_PORT) OVER (ORDER BY sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS window_column FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.NAME = 'aurum-xenon'), avg_cte AS (SELECT AVG(FROM_PORT) AS avg_from_port FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.NAME, i.DESCRIPTION, i.USER_ID, i.PROJECT_ID, i.PROTOCOL, i.FROM_PORT, i.TO_PORT, i.CIDR, i.window_column, (i.FROM_PORT - a.avg_from_port) AS deviation_from_avg_from_port FROM inner_cte AS i CROSS JOIN avg_cte AS a), q2 AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sgr.PROTOCOL, sgr.FROM_PORT, SUM(sgr.FROM_PORT) OVER (PARTITION BY sgr.PROTOCOL ORDER BY sgr.FROM_PORT) AS window_column FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.NAME = 'aurum-xenon'), ProtocolAverages AS (SELECT sgr.PROTOCOL, AVG(sgr.FROM_PORT * 1.0) AS avg_from_port FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.NAME = 'aurum-xenon' GROUP BY sgr.PROTOCOL) SELECT i.security_group_name, i.PROTOCOL, i.FROM_PORT, i.window_column FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN ProtocolAverages AS pa ON pa.PROTOCOL = i.PROTOCOL WHERE i.FROM_PORT > pa.avg_from_port) SELECT q1.NAME AS security_group_name, q1.DESCRIPTION, q1.USER_ID, q1.PROJECT_ID, q1.PROTOCOL, q1.FROM_PORT, q1.TO_PORT, q1.CIDR, q1.window_column AS min_from_port_window_3_preceding_1_following, q1.deviation_from_avg_from_port, q2.window_column AS running_sum_from_ports_within_protocol FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.NAME = q2.security_group_name AND q1.PROTOCOL = q2.PROTOCOL AND q1.FROM_PORT = q2.FROM_PORT ORDER BY q1.PROTOCOL, q1.FROM_PORT

target_disjoint_workload.question: For security group rules belonging to the security group named "aurum-xenon", and only if that security group is among the top 10 security groups with the most non-deleted rules, show the security group name, the rule protocol, the rule from port, the running sum of from ports within each protocol ordered by from port, the group’s total rule count, and a normalized metric (running sum divided by rule count) rounded to 2 decimals.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH RuleWindow AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sgr.PROTOCOL, sgr.FROM_PORT, SUM(sgr.FROM_PORT) OVER (PARTITION BY sgr.PROTOCOL ORDER BY sgr.FROM_PORT) AS window_column FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.NAME = 'aurum-xenon'), TopRuleCounts AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, COUNT(sgr.ID) AS rule_count FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.DELETED = 0 AND sgr.DELETED = 0 GROUP BY sg.NAME ORDER BY rule_count DESC LIMIT 10) SELECT rw.security_group_name, rw.PROTOCOL, rw.FROM_PORT, rw.window_column, trc.rule_count, ROUND(rw.window_column / NULLIF(trc.rule_count, 0), 2) AS normalized_running_from_port_per_rule FROM RuleWindow AS rw JOIN TopRuleCounts AS trc ON rw.security_group_name = trc.security_group_name ORDER BY normalized_running_from_port_per_rule DESC, rw.PROTOCOL, rw.FROM_PORT

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group that has tcp rules, list the security group ID, name, and description, along with (1) the number of tcp security group rules and the total of their TO_PORT values, and (2) the geometric mean of rule port-range sizes (TO_PORT − FROM_PORT + 1) across its rules where TO_PORT is at least FROM_PORT. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH TcpRuleStats AS (SELECT sg.ID AS security_group_id, sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sg.DESCRIPTION AS security_group_description, COUNT(sgr.ID) AS rule_count, SUM(sgr.TO_PORT) AS total_to_port FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.ID, sg.NAME, sg.DESCRIPTION), GeoMeanPortRange AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, EXP(AVG(LN(sgr.TO_PORT - sgr.FROM_PORT + 1))) AS geometric_mean_port_range_size FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.TO_PORT >= sgr.FROM_PORT GROUP BY sg.NAME ORDER BY geometric_mean_port_range_size DESC), CombinedSecurityGroupMetrics AS (SELECT t.security_group_id, t.security_group_name, t.security_group_description, t.rule_count, t.total_to_port, g.geometric_mean_port_range_size FROM TcpRuleStats AS t JOIN GeoMeanPortRange AS g ON t.security_group_name = g.security_group_name) SELECT security_group_id, security_group_name, security_group_description, rule_count, total_to_port, geometric_mean_port_range_size FROM CombinedSecurityGroupMetrics ORDER BY security_group_name

target_disjoint_workload.question: For security group rules belonging to the security group named "aurum-xenon" (and only if that security group has more than 100 total TCP ports covered), list the security group name, rule protocol, from port, to port, CIDR, the average from port over a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows (partitioned by protocol and ordered by from port), the total TCP ports covered for the security group, and a normalized ratio of the windowed average from port divided by the total TCP ports covered.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH RuleWindow AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sgr.PROTOCOL, sgr.FROM_PORT, sgr.TO_PORT, sgr.CIDR, AVG(sgr.FROM_PORT) OVER (PARTITION BY sgr.PROTOCOL ORDER BY sgr.FROM_PORT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING) AS window_column FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.NAME = 'aurum-xenon' ORDER BY sgr.FROM_PORT), TcpPortCoverage AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, SUM(sgr.TO_PORT - sgr.FROM_PORT + 1) AS total_ports_covered FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.NAME HAVING SUM(sgr.TO_PORT - sgr.FROM_PORT + 1) > 100) SELECT rw.security_group_name, rw.PROTOCOL, rw.FROM_PORT, rw.TO_PORT, rw.CIDR, rw.window_column AS avg_from_port_window_2_pre_2_fol, tpc.total_ports_covered, ROUND(rw.window_column / NULLIF(tpc.total_ports_covered, 0), 6) AS normalized_window_avg_to_total_ports_ratio FROM RuleWindow AS rw JOIN TcpPortCoverage AS tpc ON rw.security_group_name = tpc.security_group_name WHERE rw.security_group_name = 'aurum-xenon' ORDER BY normalized_window_avg_to_total_ports_ratio DESC, rw.FROM_PORT

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group name whose total number of ports covered across its TCP rules is greater than 100, list the security group name and total ports covered, but only include those security groups whose total ports covered is greater than the average total ports covered across all such security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, SUM(sgr.TO_PORT - sgr.FROM_PORT + 1) AS total_ports_covered FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.NAME HAVING SUM(sgr.TO_PORT - sgr.FROM_PORT + 1) > 100) SELECT security_group_name, total_ports_covered FROM inner_cte WHERE total_ports_covered > (SELECT AVG(total_ports_covered) FROM inner_cte)

target_disjoint_workload.question: For security group rules whose parent security group has the name "aurum-xenon", list the rule protocol and a rule activity status ("Active" if the rule is not deleted and "Inactive" otherwise), along with the number of rules in each category. Include subtotals for each protocol and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sgr.PROTOCOL AS rule_protocol, sgr.CIDR AS rule_cidr, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY sgr.CIDR ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS window_column FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.NAME = 'aurum-xenon'), RuleStatusCounts AS (SELECT ic.rule_protocol, CASE WHEN sgr2.DELETED = 0 THEN 'Active' ELSE 'Inactive' END AS rule_status, COUNT(*) AS total_rules FROM inner_cte AS ic JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr2 ON sgr2.CIDR = ic.rule_cidr AND sgr2.PROTOCOL = ic.rule_protocol GROUP BY ic.rule_protocol, rule_status) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(rule_protocol) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE rule_protocol END AS rule_protocol, CASE WHEN GROUPING(rule_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(rule_protocol) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE rule_status END AS rule_status, SUM(total_rules) AS total_rules FROM RuleStatusCounts GROUP BY rule_protocol, rule_status WITH ROLLUP

target_disjoint_workload.question: For security group rules that use the tcp protocol, list the security group ID, security group name, rule ID, rule CIDR, and the rank of each rule within its security group ordered by rule ID, but only keep those rules whose rule ID is greater than the average rule ID among all such tcp rules for services where the binary is 'nova-scheduler'. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.ID AS security_group_id, sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sgr.ID AS rule_id, sgr.CIDR AS rule_cidr, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sg.ID ORDER BY sgr.ID) AS window_column FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID JOIN `services` AS s ON s.`binary` = 'nova-scheduler' WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp') SELECT security_group_id, security_group_name, rule_id, rule_cidr, window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE rule_id > (SELECT AVG(rule_id) FROM inner_cte)

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group, list the security group name and its coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of rule port-range sizes (standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of (to_port − from_port) divided by the average of (to_port − from_port)), but only return those security groups whose coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) is greater than the overall average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all non-deleted security groups and non-deleted rules, considering only enabled instance types (instance_types.disabled = false). Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.name, STDDEV(sgr.to_port - sgr.from_port) / NULLIF(AVG(sgr.to_port - sgr.from_port), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.id = sgr.parent_group_id JOIN `instance_types` AS it ON 1 = 1 WHERE sg.deleted = 0 AND sgr.deleted = 0 AND it.disabled = FALSE GROUP BY sg.name HAVING AVG(sgr.to_port - sgr.from_port) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC), OverallAvg AS (SELECT AVG(inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_cov FROM inner_cte) SELECT inner_cte.name, inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte WHERE inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation > (SELECT avg_cov FROM OverallAvg) ORDER BY inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation DESC

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each non-deleted security group and rule protocol where the maximum “to” port across its rules is greater than the average of the per-(security group, protocol) maximum “to” ports (computed across all non-deleted security groups), list the security group name, the protocol, that maximum “to” port, and (for tcp rules) the range and variance of the “from” port values for the same security group. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH MaxToPortByGroupProtocol AS (SELECT sg.NAME, MAX(sgr.TO_PORT) AS max_to_port, sgr.PROTOCOL FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.DELETED = 0 GROUP BY sg.NAME, sgr.PROTOCOL HAVING MAX(sgr.TO_PORT) > 1000), TcpFromPortStatsByGroup AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, MAX(sgr.FROM_PORT) - MIN(sgr.FROM_PORT) AS from_port_range, VARIANCE(sgr.FROM_PORT) AS from_port_variance FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.NAME ORDER BY from_port_range DESC) SELECT mtp.NAME AS security_group_name, mtp.PROTOCOL, mtp.max_to_port, tfs.from_port_range, tfs.from_port_variance FROM MaxToPortByGroupProtocol AS mtp JOIN TcpFromPortStatsByGroup AS tfs ON mtp.NAME = tfs.security_group_name ORDER BY mtp.max_to_port DESC), AvgOfMaxToPortsByProtocol AS (SELECT i.PROTOCOL, AVG(i.max_to_port * 1.0) AS avg_max_to_port FROM inner_cte AS i GROUP BY i.PROTOCOL) SELECT i.security_group_name, i.PROTOCOL, i.max_to_port, i.from_port_range, i.from_port_variance FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN AvgOfMaxToPortsByProtocol AS a ON a.PROTOCOL = i.PROTOCOL WHERE i.max_to_port > (SELECT a2.avg_max_to_port FROM AvgOfMaxToPortsByProtocol AS a2 WHERE a2.PROTOCOL = i.PROTOCOL) ORDER BY i.PROTOCOL, i.max_to_port DESC

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group and rule protocol, list the security group name, description, project ID, the rule protocol, and the number of non-deleted rules. Also include subtotals per security group and a grand total, considering only non-deleted groups and rules. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME, sg.DESCRIPTION, sg.PROJECT_ID, sgr.PROTOCOL, sgr.FROM_PORT, sgr.TO_PORT, sgr.CIDR, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sg.ID ORDER BY sgr.ID) AS window_column FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.DELETED = 0 AND sgr.DELETED = 0), RuleCounts AS (SELECT NAME, DESCRIPTION, PROJECT_ID, PROTOCOL, COUNT(*) AS total_rules FROM inner_cte GROUP BY NAME, DESCRIPTION, PROJECT_ID, PROTOCOL) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(NAME) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE NAME END AS security_group_name, CASE WHEN GROUPING(DESCRIPTION) = 1 AND GROUPING(NAME) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE DESCRIPTION END AS security_group_description, CASE WHEN GROUPING(PROJECT_ID) = 1 AND GROUPING(NAME) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE PROJECT_ID END AS project_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(PROTOCOL) = 1 AND GROUPING(NAME) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE PROTOCOL END AS protocol, SUM(total_rules) AS total_rules FROM RuleCounts GROUP BY NAME, DESCRIPTION, PROJECT_ID, PROTOCOL WITH ROLLUP

target_disjoint_workload.question: For the security group named "aurum-xenon", return only those rules whose from-port is greater than the average from-port for their protocol, and for each such rule show the security group name, description, user ID, project ID, protocol, from port, to port, CIDR, the minimum from port over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following rule rows (ordered by the parent group ID), the rule’s deviation from the overall average from port across all "aurum-xenon" rules, and the running sum of from ports within the same protocol ordered by from port. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH q1 AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME, sg.DESCRIPTION, sg.USER_ID, sg.PROJECT_ID, sgr.PROTOCOL, sgr.FROM_PORT, sgr.TO_PORT, sgr.CIDR, MIN(sgr.FROM_PORT) OVER (ORDER BY sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS window_column FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.NAME = 'aurum-xenon'), avg_cte AS (SELECT AVG(FROM_PORT) AS avg_from_port FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.NAME, i.DESCRIPTION, i.USER_ID, i.PROJECT_ID, i.PROTOCOL, i.FROM_PORT, i.TO_PORT, i.CIDR, i.window_column, (i.FROM_PORT - a.avg_from_port) AS deviation_from_avg_from_port FROM inner_cte AS i CROSS JOIN avg_cte AS a), q2 AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sgr.PROTOCOL, sgr.FROM_PORT, SUM(sgr.FROM_PORT) OVER (PARTITION BY sgr.PROTOCOL ORDER BY sgr.FROM_PORT) AS window_column FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.NAME = 'aurum-xenon'), ProtocolAverages AS (SELECT sgr.PROTOCOL, AVG(sgr.FROM_PORT * 1.0) AS avg_from_port FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.NAME = 'aurum-xenon' GROUP BY sgr.PROTOCOL) SELECT i.security_group_name, i.PROTOCOL, i.FROM_PORT, i.window_column FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN ProtocolAverages AS pa ON pa.PROTOCOL = i.PROTOCOL WHERE i.FROM_PORT > pa.avg_from_port) SELECT q1.NAME AS security_group_name, q1.DESCRIPTION, q1.USER_ID, q1.PROJECT_ID, q1.PROTOCOL, q1.FROM_PORT, q1.TO_PORT, q1.CIDR, q1.window_column AS min_from_port_window_3_preceding_1_following, q1.deviation_from_avg_from_port, q2.window_column AS running_sum_from_ports_within_protocol FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.NAME = q2.security_group_name AND q1.PROTOCOL = q2.PROTOCOL AND q1.FROM_PORT = q2.FROM_PORT ORDER BY q1.PROTOCOL, q1.FROM_PORT

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group and tcp-rule CIDR, list the security group ID, name, and description, the CIDR, and the number of tcp rules and total TO_PORT across those rules. Include subtotals per security group and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.ID AS security_group_id, sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sg.DESCRIPTION AS security_group_description, COUNT(sgr.ID) AS rule_count, SUM(sgr.TO_PORT) AS total_to_port FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.ID, sg.NAME, sg.DESCRIPTION), CidrBreakdown AS (SELECT sg.ID AS security_group_id, sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sg.DESCRIPTION AS security_group_description, sgr.CIDR AS cidr, COUNT(sgr.ID) AS cidr_rule_count, SUM(sgr.TO_PORT) AS cidr_total_to_port FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID JOIN inner_cte AS i ON i.security_group_id = sg.ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.ID, sg.NAME, sg.DESCRIPTION, sgr.CIDR) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(security_group_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE security_group_id END AS security_group_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(security_group_name) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE security_group_name END AS security_group_name, CASE WHEN GROUPING(security_group_description) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE security_group_description END AS security_group_description, CASE WHEN GROUPING(cidr) = 1 AND GROUPING(security_group_id) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(cidr) = 1 AND GROUPING(security_group_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE cidr END AS cidr, SUM(cidr_rule_count) AS rule_count, SUM(cidr_total_to_port) AS total_to_port FROM CidrBreakdown GROUP BY security_group_id, security_group_name, security_group_description, cidr WITH ROLLUP

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group, list the security group name and its coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of rule port-range sizes (standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of (to_port − from_port) divided by the average of (to_port − from_port)), but only return those security groups whose coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) is greater than the overall average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all non-deleted security groups and non-deleted rules, considering only enabled instance types (instance_types.disabled = false). Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.name, STDDEV(sgr.to_port - sgr.from_port) / NULLIF(AVG(sgr.to_port - sgr.from_port), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.id = sgr.parent_group_id JOIN `instance_types` AS it ON 1 = 1 WHERE sg.deleted = 0 AND sgr.deleted = 0 AND it.disabled = FALSE GROUP BY sg.name HAVING AVG(sgr.to_port - sgr.from_port) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC), OverallAvg AS (SELECT AVG(inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_cov FROM inner_cte) SELECT inner_cte.name, inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte WHERE inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation > (SELECT avg_cov FROM OverallAvg) ORDER BY inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation DESC

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each non-deleted security group and rule protocol where the maximum “to” port across its rules is greater than the average of the per-(security group, protocol) maximum “to” ports (computed across all non-deleted security groups), list the security group name, the protocol, that maximum “to” port, and (for tcp rules) the range and variance of the “from” port values for the same security group. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH MaxToPortByGroupProtocol AS (SELECT sg.NAME, MAX(sgr.TO_PORT) AS max_to_port, sgr.PROTOCOL FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.DELETED = 0 GROUP BY sg.NAME, sgr.PROTOCOL HAVING MAX(sgr.TO_PORT) > 1000), TcpFromPortStatsByGroup AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, MAX(sgr.FROM_PORT) - MIN(sgr.FROM_PORT) AS from_port_range, VARIANCE(sgr.FROM_PORT) AS from_port_variance FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.NAME ORDER BY from_port_range DESC) SELECT mtp.NAME AS security_group_name, mtp.PROTOCOL, mtp.max_to_port, tfs.from_port_range, tfs.from_port_variance FROM MaxToPortByGroupProtocol AS mtp JOIN TcpFromPortStatsByGroup AS tfs ON mtp.NAME = tfs.security_group_name ORDER BY mtp.max_to_port DESC), AvgOfMaxToPortsByProtocol AS (SELECT i.PROTOCOL, AVG(i.max_to_port * 1.0) AS avg_max_to_port FROM inner_cte AS i GROUP BY i.PROTOCOL) SELECT i.security_group_name, i.PROTOCOL, i.max_to_port, i.from_port_range, i.from_port_variance FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN AvgOfMaxToPortsByProtocol AS a ON a.PROTOCOL = i.PROTOCOL WHERE i.max_to_port > (SELECT a2.avg_max_to_port FROM AvgOfMaxToPortsByProtocol AS a2 WHERE a2.PROTOCOL = i.PROTOCOL) ORDER BY i.PROTOCOL, i.max_to_port DESC

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group and rule protocol where the maximum “to” port across its non-deleted rules is greater than 1000, list the security group name, the protocol, that maximum “to” port, and the (for tcp rules) range and variance of the “from” port values for the same security group. Do not repeat the security group name if it is the same as the previous row, and include a subtotal row per security group showing the total number of qualifying protocols and the overall maximum “to” port for that group. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH MaxToPortByGroupProtocol AS (SELECT sg.NAME, MAX(sgr.TO_PORT) AS max_to_port, sgr.PROTOCOL FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.DELETED = 0 GROUP BY sg.NAME, sgr.PROTOCOL HAVING MAX(sgr.TO_PORT) > 1000), TcpFromPortStatsByGroup AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, MAX(sgr.FROM_PORT) - MIN(sgr.FROM_PORT) AS from_port_range, VARIANCE(sgr.FROM_PORT) AS from_port_variance FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.NAME ORDER BY from_port_range DESC) SELECT mtp.NAME AS security_group_name, mtp.PROTOCOL, mtp.max_to_port, tfs.from_port_range, tfs.from_port_variance FROM MaxToPortByGroupProtocol AS mtp JOIN TcpFromPortStatsByGroup AS tfs ON mtp.NAME = tfs.security_group_name ORDER BY mtp.max_to_port DESC) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(security_group_name) OVER (ORDER BY sg_sort, security_group_name, protocol) = security_group_name THEN NULL ELSE security_group_name END AS security_group_name, protocol, max_to_port, from_port_range, from_port_variance, qualifying_protocols FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.security_group_name) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.security_group_name END AS sg_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.security_group_name) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.security_group_name END AS security_group_name, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.security_group_name) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE i.PROTOCOL END AS protocol, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.security_group_name) = 1 THEN MAX(i.max_to_port) ELSE i.max_to_port END AS max_to_port, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.security_group_name) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE i.from_port_range END AS from_port_range, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.security_group_name) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE i.from_port_variance END AS from_port_variance, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.security_group_name) = 1 THEN COUNT(*) ELSE NULL END AS qualifying_protocols FROM inner_cte AS i GROUP BY i.security_group_name, i.PROTOCOL, i.max_to_port, i.from_port_range, i.from_port_variance WITH ROLLUP) AS tbltmp ORDER BY sg_sort, security_group_name, protocol

target_disjoint_workload.question: For security group rules belonging to the security group named "aurum-xenon", and only if that security group is among the top 10 security groups with the most non-deleted rules, show the security group name, the rule protocol, the rule from port, the running sum of from ports within each protocol ordered by from port, the group’s total rule count, and a normalized metric (running sum divided by rule count) rounded to 2 decimals.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH RuleWindow AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sgr.PROTOCOL, sgr.FROM_PORT, SUM(sgr.FROM_PORT) OVER (PARTITION BY sgr.PROTOCOL ORDER BY sgr.FROM_PORT) AS window_column FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.NAME = 'aurum-xenon'), TopRuleCounts AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, COUNT(sgr.ID) AS rule_count FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.DELETED = 0 AND sgr.DELETED = 0 GROUP BY sg.NAME ORDER BY rule_count DESC LIMIT 10) SELECT rw.security_group_name, rw.PROTOCOL, rw.FROM_PORT, rw.window_column, trc.rule_count, ROUND(rw.window_column / NULLIF(trc.rule_count, 0), 2) AS normalized_running_from_port_per_rule FROM RuleWindow AS rw JOIN TopRuleCounts AS trc ON rw.security_group_name = trc.security_group_name ORDER BY normalized_running_from_port_per_rule DESC, rw.PROTOCOL, rw.FROM_PORT

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group that has tcp rules, list the security group ID, name, and description, along with (1) the number of tcp security group rules and the total of their TO_PORT values, and (2) the geometric mean of rule port-range sizes (TO_PORT − FROM_PORT + 1) across its rules where TO_PORT is at least FROM_PORT. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH TcpRuleStats AS (SELECT sg.ID AS security_group_id, sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sg.DESCRIPTION AS security_group_description, COUNT(sgr.ID) AS rule_count, SUM(sgr.TO_PORT) AS total_to_port FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.ID, sg.NAME, sg.DESCRIPTION), GeoMeanPortRange AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, EXP(AVG(LN(sgr.TO_PORT - sgr.FROM_PORT + 1))) AS geometric_mean_port_range_size FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.TO_PORT >= sgr.FROM_PORT GROUP BY sg.NAME ORDER BY geometric_mean_port_range_size DESC), CombinedSecurityGroupMetrics AS (SELECT t.security_group_id, t.security_group_name, t.security_group_description, t.rule_count, t.total_to_port, g.geometric_mean_port_range_size FROM TcpRuleStats AS t JOIN GeoMeanPortRange AS g ON t.security_group_name = g.security_group_name) SELECT security_group_id, security_group_name, security_group_description, rule_count, total_to_port, geometric_mean_port_range_size FROM CombinedSecurityGroupMetrics ORDER BY security_group_name

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group name and its TCP “from port” variability status (High if the from-port range is at least 1000, otherwise Low)—including subtotals per security group name and a grand total—show the total number of security groups in that category and how many qualifying (non-deleted) security group rules belong to that security group where the security group’s id is greater than the average id across all non-deleted security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH sg_tcp_from_port_variability_rollup AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, MAX(sgr.FROM_PORT) - MIN(sgr.FROM_PORT) AS from_port_range, VARIANCE(sgr.FROM_PORT) AS from_port_variance FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.NAME ORDER BY from_port_range DESC), RangeStatus AS (SELECT security_group_name, CASE WHEN from_port_range >= 1000 THEN 'High' ELSE 'Low' END AS variability_status, COUNT(*) AS total_security_groups FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_name, variability_status) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(security_group_name) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE security_group_name END AS security_group_name, CASE WHEN GROUPING(variability_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(security_group_name) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE variability_status END AS variability_status, SUM(total_security_groups) AS total_security_groups FROM RangeStatus GROUP BY security_group_name, variability_status WITH ROLLUP), sg_rule_details_with_max_next_2 AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME, sgr.PROTOCOL, sgr.FROM_PORT, sgr.TO_PORT, sgr.CIDR, sgr.ID AS RULE_ID, MAX(sg.ID) OVER (ORDER BY sgr.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING) AS MAX_GROUP_ID_NEXT_2 FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.DELETED = 0) SELECT i.NAME, i.PROTOCOL, i.FROM_PORT, i.TO_PORT, i.CIDR, i.RULE_ID, i.MAX_GROUP_ID_NEXT_2 FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN `security_groups` AS sg2 ON sg2.NAME = i.NAME WHERE sg2.DELETED = 0 AND sg2.ID > (SELECT AVG(sg3.ID) * 1.0 FROM `security_groups` AS sg3 WHERE sg3.DELETED = 0)) SELECT v.security_group_name, v.variability_status, v.total_security_groups, COUNT(r.RULE_ID) AS qualifying_rule_count FROM sg_tcp_from_port_variability_rollup AS v LEFT JOIN sg_rule_details_with_max_next_2 AS r ON r.NAME = v.security_group_name GROUP BY v.security_group_name, v.variability_status, v.total_security_groups ORDER BY v.security_group_name, v.variability_status

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group name whose total number of ports covered across its TCP rules is greater than 100, list the security group name and total ports covered, but only include those security groups whose total ports covered is greater than the average total ports covered across all such security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, SUM(sgr.TO_PORT - sgr.FROM_PORT + 1) AS total_ports_covered FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.NAME HAVING SUM(sgr.TO_PORT - sgr.FROM_PORT + 1) > 100) SELECT security_group_name, total_ports_covered FROM inner_cte WHERE total_ports_covered > (SELECT AVG(total_ports_covered) FROM inner_cte)

target_disjoint_workload.question: For security group rules whose parent security group has the name "aurum-xenon", list the rule protocol and a rule activity status ("Active" if the rule is not deleted and "Inactive" otherwise), along with the number of rules in each category. Include subtotals for each protocol and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sgr.PROTOCOL AS rule_protocol, sgr.CIDR AS rule_cidr, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY sgr.CIDR ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS window_column FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sg.NAME = 'aurum-xenon'), RuleStatusCounts AS (SELECT ic.rule_protocol, CASE WHEN sgr2.DELETED = 0 THEN 'Active' ELSE 'Inactive' END AS rule_status, COUNT(*) AS total_rules FROM inner_cte AS ic JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr2 ON sgr2.CIDR = ic.rule_cidr AND sgr2.PROTOCOL = ic.rule_protocol GROUP BY ic.rule_protocol, rule_status) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(rule_protocol) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE rule_protocol END AS rule_protocol, CASE WHEN GROUPING(rule_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(rule_protocol) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE rule_status END AS rule_status, SUM(total_rules) AS total_rules FROM RuleStatusCounts GROUP BY rule_protocol, rule_status WITH ROLLUP

target_disjoint_workload.question: For each security group name, among only 'tcp' rules, list the security group name, the variance of the starting port (FROM_PORT), and the total number of tcp rules, keeping only security groups whose tcp rule count is greater than the average tcp rule count across all security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, VARIANCE(sgr.FROM_PORT) AS from_port_variance FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.NAME ORDER BY from_port_variance DESC), tcp_rule_counts AS (SELECT sg.NAME AS security_group_name, COUNT(*) AS tcp_rule_count FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp' GROUP BY sg.NAME), avg_tcp_rule_count AS (SELECT AVG(tcp_rule_count * 1.0) AS avg_tcp_rule_count FROM tcp_rule_counts) SELECT i.security_group_name, i.from_port_variance, trc.tcp_rule_count FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN tcp_rule_counts AS trc ON i.security_group_name = trc.security_group_name CROSS JOIN avg_tcp_rule_count AS a WHERE trc.tcp_rule_count > a.avg_tcp_rule_count ORDER BY i.from_port_variance DESC

target_disjoint_workload.question: For security group rules that use the tcp protocol, list the security group ID, security group name, rule ID, rule CIDR, and the rank of each rule within its security group ordered by rule ID, but only keep those rules whose rule ID is greater than the average rule ID among all such tcp rules for services where the binary is 'nova-scheduler'. Do not return any rounded answers.
target_disjoint_workload.sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT sg.ID AS security_group_id, sg.NAME AS security_group_name, sgr.ID AS rule_id, sgr.CIDR AS rule_cidr, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sg.ID ORDER BY sgr.ID) AS window_column FROM `security_groups` AS sg JOIN `security_group_rules` AS sgr ON sg.ID = sgr.PARENT_GROUP_ID JOIN `services` AS s ON s.`binary` = 'nova-scheduler' WHERE sgr.PROTOCOL = 'tcp') SELECT security_group_id, security_group_name, rule_id, rule_cidr, window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE rule_id > (SELECT AVG(rule_id) FROM inner_cte)
